notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production inference of clinical summarization + patient support chatbot. Primary drivers: predictable latency for real-time triage, tenant isolation because PHI may be processed, and reserved GPU pool for guaranteed throughput during peak clinic hours.

Requirements & asks (shorthand):
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 120ms for short chat responses (<=256 tokens), p99 < 400ms acceptable for long summarizations (<=2k tokens) — WHY: triage flow times are SLAs with operations.
- Throughput targets: steady-state 250 token QPS, 10x burst to 2.5k token QPS for morning huddle windows. Want guaranteed burst reserves or predictable throttling.
- Reserved GPUs: SE asked for sizing calc. Initial ask: 4x A10G-equivalent for POC (estimate), plan to scale to 12-16 for prod with autoscale headroom. Need explicit GPU reservation and priority lanes so other tenants on Dedicated pool can't cause latency spikes.
- Traffic shaping & priority lanes: customer wants per-route quotas + priority tagging (e.g., "triage" lane vs "batch-summarize" lane). Must support preemptive QoS: high-priority requests should preempt batching/cold start tasks and have guaranteed slot in scheduler. Interested in rate-limiter that is token-aware and can enforce per-route p95 budgets.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: require strict isolation policies, per-tenant CPU/GPU cgroups or dedicated MIG partitions; agreement that Redwood will throttle misbehaving customer workloads and surface metrics.
- Security/compliance: VPC-only control plane, customer-managed KMS for keys, audit log retention 3 years, SAML SSO + SCIM. Data residency: US-only for PHI.

POC plan & metrics:
- Week 1: deploy private control plane in VPC, KMS test, run low-volume chat flows.
- Week 2: scaled load test with morning-burst pattern (replicate clinic peaks). Key success: sustained p95 latency under 120ms for priority lane during 10x bursts, no >10% increase in cost-per-token vs baseline.

Quote from Dir. of ML Ops: "We need hard guarantees — if a lane is marked priority, it should behave like it's on its own fleet. No surprises during clinic hours."

Negotiation points open: SLA latency tiers (penalty structure), minimum committed GPUs vs burst credits, SLO measurement windows, telemetry export format to Splunk, and contract language for noisy-neighbor mitigation.
